md_alberton_rock.blurb: Alberton Rock is a roughly 50-foot cliff in Patapsco Valley State Park, west of Baltimore, with ten top-rope lines. Grades start around 5.6 and cluster in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, with a pair of 5.11s up the big roof feature in the middle. It suits beginners, families and anyone setting up their first top-rope anchors. The trees sit well back from the edge, so bring a long anchor system and a rope of about 65 feet. The cliff is hidden by foliage in summer and the base can get briery. Boulders line the trail in, and copperheads have been seen near the top.
md_alberton_rock.approach: An easy walk of about 0.6 mile along a trail and old road from the parking lot, passing a few boulders; the base sits right beside the trail.

md_frameshift_boulder.blurb: Frameshift Boulder is the first boulder you meet on the trail into the Alberton Boulders in Patapsco Valley State Park, near Baltimore. It stands about 15 to 20 feet tall and sits almost on the path, half hidden by vegetation, so it is easy to walk past. Ten problems are packed onto it: a handful of V0 and easier lines on the left, a couple around V4, and a few much harder projects up toward V9 and V10 on the right. Bring pads and a spotter. Stumps and a small pipe in the landings are hazards, and the top-outs can be prickly.
md_frameshift_boulder.approach: Walk roughly 100 meters past the park entrance sign and gate; the boulder is on the right, beside the trail.

md_stoned_sphere_boulder.blurb: Stoned Sphere Boulder is one of the blocks in the Fallston Boulder Garden, a shady, secluded bouldering spot along the Little Gunpowder River northeast of Baltimore. Despite the name it is not round. Ten problems here, mostly easy to moderate, with a good handful of V0 and V1 lines, a few V2 and V3, and a single hard project near V7. The faces lean northwest, which keeps things cool in warm weather. There is no real trail at the boulder; you scramble up and around its right side and back down toward the water. The left face is somewhat overgrown.

md_tower_of_babylon.blurb: Tower of Babylon is a steep, squared-off pillar in the Black Rock cliffs on the South Mountain ridge, reached by a hike on the Appalachian Trail. Ten routes, split evenly between trad and top-rope, run from about 5.6 to 5.12, with half of them around 5.10. The faces have small overhangs and slots, and a few deeper roofs. Belays are from a scree field at the base, where loose rock is a concern, so wear a helmet. The main face looks west, and the south side holds the shorter, well-liked 5.10 line.
md_tower_of_babylon.approach: From the trailhead, hike about 0.9 mile uphill to the Appalachian Trail, then south about 0.6 mile to an unmarked side trail just north of the Black Rock overlook trail. It leads west to the top of the tower; alternatively follow the cliff line south to a drainage that drops to the scree field at the base.
